failure_details: 0 llm_unsupported: CEO Cristiano Amon reportedly said prices would rise from September.: No citation given; the sentence is unfinished and cites no evidence.
1 llm_unsupported: Qualcomm's news-reported comments mostly matched its formal guidance.: Evidence shows no matching overall assessment; comparisons are mostly not_comparable or no_formal_guidance.

1 llm_unsupported: Reported comment that Q4 adjusted earnings would be below Wall Street expectations was excluded as wrong.: Cited item shows it was reviewed as wrong and left out, but the claim's wording is an exclusi
2 llm_unsupported: Q4 revenue comment ($9.7B to $10.5B) matched formal guidance issued July 29.: Revenue comparison is marked pending, not consistent.
scores.answer:
Two of Qualcomm's news-reported numeric comments were checked against formal guidance and matched it. The rest could not be compared. - **Matched:** Reported comments on fourth-quarter adjusted EPS ($2.05 to $2.25) and revenue ($9.7 billion to $10.5 billion) were marked consistent with the formal guidance issued July 29 (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [1][2]. - **Apple modem decline:** Qualcomm reportedly said Apple-modem revenue would decline faster than previously expected, starting in its fiscal fourth quarter (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [3]. The earnings call reportedly described an "acceleration" in the Apple revenue dip (reported by theverge.com) [4]. The formal release gives only segment ranges: QCT revenue of $8.4 billion to $9.0 billion and QTL revenue of $1.2 billion to $1.4 billion [2]. None is Apple-specific, so there is no formal figure to compare these comments against. - **Other directional comments:** Reported comments included non-handset growth offsetting Apple losses, FY2027 top-line growth, and a $5 billion AI data center revenue goal by fiscal 2027 and $15 billion by fiscal 2029 (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [3][5]. None has a formal figure to compare against. - **Price increases:** CEO Cristiano Amon reportedly said product prices "are going to go up" starting September 1 (reported by theverge.com) [6]. No formal guidance covers prices. - **Q4 earnings comment:** A reported comment that fourth-quarter adjusted earnings would fall below Wall Street expectations is marked by the tool as "reviewed as wrong" and left out of the outcome counts (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [3]. The statement list has 10 more claims that I did not retrieve, so this covers only the claims shown.

scores.question: What did Meta's executives say about 2025 capex, and how did actual capex compare?
notes: does not say management made no such claim
failure_details: 0 numbers_cited: a sentence with a number has no citation: That $72.2 billion figure does not match the latest 10-K capex line of $69.7 billion, so the two numbers are on different bases or have been revised.
1 llm_unsupported: Filings searched do not explain the difference: Cited evidence does not state what filings were searched; claim about search is not in E1, E9, or E10
1 llm_unsupported: No management statements about 2025 capex turned up in stored news: No news item is cited; claim about absence of news has no evidence
scores.answer:
Meta's formal 2025 capex guidance was raised several times during the year. The Q3 2025 release gave the latest range: "We currently expect 2025 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $70-72 billion, increased from our prior outlook of $66-72 billion" [1]. Earlier ranges were $64-72 billion in Q1 [2], $66-72 billion in Q2 [3], and $60-65 billion in the January 2025 release [4].
The actual figure in the FY2025 10-K is $69,691M [5]. That is $309M below the low end of the final $70-72 billion range [1][5]. The guidance tool compared the ranges against a first-reported actual of $72,215M [1], so the figure the guidance was judged against ($72.2 billion) differs from the $69.7 billion in the latest 10-K [1][5].

scores.answer:
Nvidia's May 20, 2026 earnings release guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China [1]. The June date is the article's date, not a confirmed statement date (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [2]. Nvidia hit the figure and exceeded it. Revenue for the quarter ended July 26, 2026 was $96,221M, per the 10-Q filed August 26, 2026 [3]. That is $5,221M above the $91.0 billion guidance point [1][3], a 5.74% beat [1][3].

scores.question: What has Tesla said in the news about its capital expenditures for 2026?
scores.answer:
Tesla's earnings releases contain no capital expenditure guidance. None of the 11 checked, through FY2026Q2, includes any [1].
The only statement I found is in a news report. Fool.com reported on October 2, 2026 that Tesla expects capital expenditures of over $25 billion in 2026, due to its AI initiatives (reported by fool.com) [2]. The article does not say who made the statement or where, so I can only attribute it to the company. The claim is pending, since the 2026 period has not been reported yet, and no formal capex guidance was issued within 45 days of it (reported by fool.com) [2].

Andy Jassy said on the July 30, 2026 earnings call that Amazon now expects to spend $220 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, due to higher memory costs, as reported by Fortune [1]. I could not confirm this figure in Amazon's own filings. The Q2 2026 earnings release and 10-Q excerpts I retrieved do not state a 2026 capex figure [2][3][4]. Amazon's earnings releases give no capex guidance for 2026 [5], so the $220 billion figure is what Jassy said on the call, not formal guidance [1]. scores.answer:
Apple's executives have not been found saying how fast iPhone Duo shipments will grow next year. The statement search returned no such quote, and the filings search returned no Duo passage [1][2][3][4][5][6]. The news reports I found cover pre-orders and delivery timing, not growth. Pre-orders reportedly sold out, and delivery dates moved from October 23 into late January [E8, reported by fool.com]. CBS News and Bloomberg headlines say Duo orders are backordered or slipping into 2027 [E17, reported by CBS News; E19, reported by Bloomberg.com]. I have only the headlines, not the full articles, and none gives a growth rate for next year. Apple's earnings releases contain no guidance at all [7]. These are not specific to Duo.
Left out because they could not be verified (a figure without a source): one statement.
